questions.questionText: What makes in-context learning different from how models in the Classical ML/Deep Learning courses learn?
options: It requires more training data than gradient descent
The model picks up a task's pattern purely from examples in the prompt, with no weight updates at all
It only works for classification tasks
It's identical to gradient descent, just renamed
questions.correctAnswer: The model picks up a task's pattern purely from examples in the prompt, with no weight updates at all
questions.explanation: Unlike every training process covered earlier in this platform, in-context learning changes nothing about the model's weights — the "learning" happens entirely within a single forward pass over the prompt.

questions.questionText: What do few-shot examples in a prompt accomplish that a zero-shot instruction alone often doesn't?
options: They clarify the exact task including edge cases, and demonstrate the expected output format more reliably than describing it in words
They permanently update the model's weights for future conversations
They reduce the number of tokens used
questions.correctAnswer: They clarify the exact task including edge cases, and demonstrate the expected output format more reliably than describing it in words
questions.explanation: Concrete input/output examples pin down ambiguous cases and formatting far more precisely than a natural-language description alone typically can.

questions.questionText: What's a real practical tradeoff of adding more few-shot examples to a prompt?
options: There is no tradeoff, more examples are always strictly better
Each example consumes context window tokens, competing with everything else you want to include in the prompt
More examples always slow down model training
Few-shot examples can only be used with certain model architectures
questions.correctAnswer: Each example consumes context window tokens, competing with everything else you want to include in the prompt
questions.explanation: Since few-shot examples occupy real tokens in a finite context window, there's a genuine tradeoff between example count and room for other context — the exact issue the context engineering lesson tackles next.
